elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The Company may assign this Agreement, without HDI's consent, to an affiliate ..." — express affiliate carve-out, consent-free, in favour of the Customer (the Company).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same sentence continues "... or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets", governed by the same "without HDI's consent" qualifier.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent" — an affirmative consent gate on the Vendor that did not exist in the original boilerplate.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" — the reasonableness standard attaches directly to the Vendor-assignment consent.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and shall never assign to a competitor of the Company" — absolute bar, not subject to the reasonableness standard. "Competitor" is undefined but the term operates only as a prohibition on HDI, so the ambiguity cannot be used against the Customer.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "A change of control of the Company shall not give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement." Consistent with Sections 4.1/4.2, which contain no change-of-control trigger, so nothing in the document contradicts it.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The redline grants a consent-free successor right only to the Company; HDI's assignments (including to a successor) all sit behind "may not assign ... without the Company's prior written consent". No mutual successor right is created.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears anywhere in amended Section 10.3; the Company's affiliate/successor assignment is simply consent-free and silent as to notice.

Consent is required only for HDI assignments. Customer assignments outside the affiliate/M&A carve-out remain ungated by any express consent requirement, so the fallback's symmetric consent gate is absent.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The only consent regime created — consent to HDI assignment — carries "which shall not be unreasonably withheld"; there is no consent right anywhere in the clause that lacks the reasonableness standard.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are expressed in operative language in the amended Section 10.3, not merely promised in the margin comment. The fallback is incomplete (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, no consent gate on Customer's other assignments), but that is irrelevant because completeness at either level suffices, and the comment correctly offers the mutual-notice construct only as a negotiating alternative.

Deviation classification is sound: the original clause is bare successors-and-assigns boilerplate with no consent gate, no notice mechanic and no reasonableness standard, so it fails the fallback on material terms; it is a deviation rather than 'missing' because a usable assignment clause exists at 10.3 to amend.

Minimal: the pre-existing successors-and-assigns sentence is retained verbatim (it is neutral-to-favourable and binds HDI's successors), and only three sentences are added, each mapping to a preferred element. No operative term is duplicated and nothing outside the ASSIGN checklist (e.g., no anti-assignment remedy, no change-of-control notice obligation, no re-pricing bar) is imported.

Preserves intent: the addition does not touch Section 4.1/4.2 termination or payment mechanics, the Section 6 exclusivity provisions, the Marks licence or the confidentiality allocation, and creates no contradiction with the retained first sentence, since an affiliate or M&A successor taking the Company's position is itself a permitted 'assign' under that sentence.

Optional hardening, not required for completeness and not a defect to repair: (a) consider deeming an HDI merger, change of control or transfer by operation of law an 'assignment' for purposes of the consent gate, otherwise HDI could reach the same result structurally; and (b) consider anchoring 'competitor of the Company' to the entities already named in the Section 6 exclusivity provisions to remove any argument about the term's scope.
